Test Description: Verifies PCIe device enumeration by performing link training, configuring cache coherency control via the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register for both PCIe controller instances, polling the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG for link-up status on both SII interfaces, reading the device Vendor ID from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, enabling IO/Memory/Bus Master access via TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG, programming memory base addresses, performing BAR sizing and configuration on BAR0_REG, BAR1_REG, SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG, SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG, MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG, and PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG for both PCIe slave endpoints, and polling a synchronization register for test completion.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Clear the synchronization register to prepare for the test. 2. Initiate PCIe link training for the configured controller mode (Root Complex or Endpoint) on both DM0 and DM1 instances. 3. Enable cache coherency by programming the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register for both PCIe controller instances, setting the required bit fields for cache control. 4. Wait for the coherency configuration to take effect. 5. Perform a combined coherency control update for both controller instances. 6. Poll the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG on SII0 interface until the link-up status bits indicate the PCIe link is established. 7. Poll the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG on SII1 interface until the link-up status bits indicate the PCIe link is established. 8. Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to retrieve the Vendor ID of the enumerated PCIe device. 9. Write to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO space, memory space, and bus master access. 10. Program memory base addresses for both DM0 and DM1 controllers. 11. Configure system-level control registers to enable PCIe subsystem operation. 12. Disable cache coherency by clearing the relevant bit fields in COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF for both controller instances. 13. Wait for the configuration to stabilize. 14. Perform BAR sizing on the downstream endpoint by writing all-ones to BAR0_REG, BAR1_REG, SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG, SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG, MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG, and PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, then reading back to determine BAR sizes. 15. Program actual BAR values for the downstream endpoint. 16. Repeat BAR sizing and programming for the second PCIe slave endpoint. 17. Poll the synchronization register until the expected completion value is observed. 18. Report test completion.
Impacted Registers: COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF; SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG; TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG; TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG; BAR0_REG; BAR1_REG; SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG; SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG; MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG; PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG on both SII0 and SII1 interfaces reports link-up status with the expected status bits set. The TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG must return a valid Vendor ID. BAR sizing must return valid size information when all-ones are written to BAR0_REG, BAR1_REG, SEC_LAT_TIMER_SUB_BUS_SEC_BUS_PRI_BUS_REG, SEC_STAT_IO_LIMIT_IO_BASE_REG, MEM_LIMIT_MEM_BASE_REG, and PREF_MEM_LIMIT_PREF_MEM_BASE_REG, and the programmed BAR values must be readable after configuration. The synchronization register must eventually return the expected completion value to indicate end-to-end test success. The test calls finish(0) to indicate pass.
Remarks: The testcase uses compile-time conditional compilation (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, DM1_EP) to select the link training mode, so behavior varies depending on the build configuration. Polling loops on both SII0 and SII1 interfaces wait indefinitely for link-up with no timeout, which may cause the test to hang if the link does not come up. Cache coherency is enabled before enumeration and disabled afterward. BAR sizing and programming is performed on two PCIe slave endpoints (slave 0 and slave 1). Six system-level control registers could not be mapped to canonical register names. One coherency control macro for the PCIE1 instance could not be resolved due to missing header definitions.

Test Description: Verifies PCIe DMA write and read data transfer across four channels on both PCIe controller instances. The test performs link training, polls the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG for link-up status, reads the device Vendor ID from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, enables IO/Memory/Bus Master access via TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG, programs BARs and memory base addresses, preloads source data into memory, unmasks DMA interrupts via DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF, sequentially programs and triggers DMA write transfers on channels 0 through 3 using DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF, waits for each transfer to complete via interrupt, then programs and triggers DMA read transfers on channels 0 through 3 using DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF, again waiting for each transfer to complete via interrupt. The interrupt handler reads DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF to determine which channels completed, then clears the interrupts via DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF. The test reports completion after all eight DMA transfers finish successfully.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Clear the synchronization register to prepare for the test. 2. Initiate PCIe link training for the configured controller mode on the selected controller instance. 3. Poll the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG on the appropriate SII interface until the link-up status bits confirm the PCIe link is established. 4. Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to retrieve the Vendor ID of the enumerated PCIe device. 5. Write to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO space, memory space, and bus master access. 6. Program BARs and memory base addresses for the selected controller. 7. Configure non-secure protection and wait for the synchronization register to indicate readiness. 8. Preload source memory with known data patterns for DMA transfer verification. 9. Enable the GIC and configure interrupt handling for DMA completion. 10. Unmask DMA write and read interrupts by writing to DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF. 11. Sequentially program and trigger DMA write transfers on channels 0 through 3 using DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF, waiting for each channel completion interrupt before proceeding to the next. 12. Sequentially program and trigger DMA read transfers on channels 0 through 3 using DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF, waiting for each channel completion interrupt before proceeding to the next. 13. In the interrupt handler, read DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF to identify completed channels, then clear the interrupts via DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF and DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF. 14. Report test completion after all DMA transfers finish successfully.
Impacted Registers: SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG; TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG; TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG; DMA_WRITE_INT_MASK_OFF; DMA_READ_INT_MASK_OFF; DMA_WRITE_DOORBELL_OFF; DMA_READ_DOORBELL_OFF; DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF; DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF; DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF; DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG reports link-up status with the expected status bits set. The TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG must return a valid Vendor ID. All four DMA write channel transfers must complete successfully, each signaled by a DMA write completion interrupt read from DMA_WRITE_INT_STATUS_OFF and cleared via DMA_WRITE_INT_CLEAR_OFF. All four DMA read channel transfers must complete successfully, each signaled by a DMA read completion interrupt read from DMA_READ_INT_STATUS_OFF and cleared via DMA_READ_INT_CLEAR_OFF. The interrupt handler must correctly identify completed channels by masking the lower 4 bits of the status registers. The test calls finish(0) to indicate pass after all eight DMA transfers complete.
Remarks: The testcase uses compile-time conditional compilation to select between DM0_RC and DM1_RC controller instances, so behavior varies depending on the build configuration. DMA transfers are performed sequentially one channel at a time, with each channel waiting for interrupt-driven completion before the next channel is triggered. The polling loop on the SII interface waits indefinitely for link-up with no timeout. Source data is preloaded with two distinct patterns for verification purposes. The GIC interrupt number differs between DM0 and DM1 instances. All DMA register macros for the PCIE1 controller instance could not be resolved due to missing header definitions. One synchronization register could not be mapped to a canonical register name.

Test Description: Verifies PCIe memory write and read data integrity through the PCIe slave interfaces. The test performs link training, configures cache coherency control via the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register for both PCIe controller instances, polls the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG for link-up status on the SII interface, reads the device Vendor ID from TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG, enables IO/Memory/Bus Master access via TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG, programs BARs and memory base addresses, signals synchronization readiness, partially disables cache coherency, then performs memory write-read verification at multiple target addresses through the PCIe slave interface. The test supports Root Complex and Endpoint modes on both controller instances and polls a synchronization register for test completion.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Clear the synchronization register to prepare for the test. 2. Initiate PCIe link training for the configured controller mode (Root Complex or Endpoint) on the selected controller instance. 3. Enable cache coherency by programming the COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF register for both PCIe controller instances, setting the required bit fields for cache control. 4. Wait for the coherency configuration to take effect. 5. Perform a combined coherency control update for both controller instances. 6. Poll the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG on the appropriate SII interface until the link-up status bits indicate the PCIe link is established. 7. Read the TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG to retrieve the Vendor ID of the enumerated PCIe device. 8. Write to TYPE1_STATUS_COMMAND_REG to enable IO space, memory space, and bus master access. 9. Program BARs and memory base addresses for the selected controller. 10. Configure non-secure protection and signal synchronization readiness. 11. Partially disable cache coherency by clearing specific bit fields in COHERENCY_CONTROL_3_OFF for both controller instances. 12. Wait for the configuration to stabilize. 13. Perform a combined cache coherency disable for both controller instances. 14. Wait for the system to stabilize after coherency changes. 15. Execute memory write-read operations at multiple target addresses through the PCIe slave interface to verify data integrity. 16. Poll the synchronization register until the expected completion value is observed. 17. Report test completion.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when the SPCIE_CAP_HEADER_REG reports link-up status with the expected status bits set on the appropriate SII interface. The TYPE1_DEV_ID_VEND_ID_REG must return a valid Vendor ID. Memory write-read operations performed through the PCIe slave interface must complete successfully, with the written data patterns verified by the memory write-read helper function at each target address. The synchronization register must eventually return the expected completion value to indicate end-to-end test success. The test calls finish(0) to indicate pass.
Remarks: The testcase uses compile-time conditional compilation (DM0_RC, DM1_RC, DM0_EP, DM1_EP, DM0, DM1) to select the controller mode and instance, so behavior varies depending on the build configuration. Cache coherency is enabled before enumeration and partially disabled afterward, with a two-phase disable sequence. The Endpoint mode uses a fixed wait instead of polling for link-up. Memory write-read operations use different data patterns and target addresses depending on the controller mode. Under Root Complex mode, three memory addresses are tested; under Endpoint mode, five BAR1 addresses are tested. The polling loop on the SII interface waits indefinitely for link-up with no timeout. One synchronization register and one coherency control macro for the PCIE1 instance could not be mapped to canonical register names due to missing definitions.

Test Description: Verifies register write-read integrity across three PCIe register domains for both controller instances. The test checks reset default values of MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, and UTILITY_OFF in the DBI controller space, SII interface registers, and PHY registers. It then performs write-read verification using multiple data patterns to validate register accessibility and data integrity across all three domains.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Read all DBI controller registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF) for both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances and verify they contain the expected reset default values. 2. Read all SII interface registers for both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances and verify reset default values. 3. Release PHY from reset by writing to the PHY reset control registers for both instances. 4. Read all PHY registers for both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances and verify reset default values. 5. Iterate through multiple test data patterns (all-ones, alternating bits, inverse alternating bits). 6. For each pattern, write the pattern to all DBI controller registers for both instances. 7. Write the pattern masked with the appropriate write mask to all SII registers for both instances. 8. Release PHY from reset and write the PHY-specific test pattern masked with the PHY write mask to all PHY registers for both instances. 9. Read back all DBI controller registers and compare with the written pattern. 10. Read back all SII registers and compare with the masked written pattern. 11. Read back all PHY registers, extract the relevant 16-bit field, and compare with the masked PHY pattern. 12. Report overall pass/fail based on accumulated error counts.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: The test passes when all DBI controller registers (MSI_CAP_OFF_08H_REG, MSI_CAP_OFF_10H_REG, FILTER_MASK_2_OFF, AXI_MSTR_MSG_ADDR_HIGH_OFF, UTILITY_OFF) for both PCIE0 and PCIE1 instances read back their expected reset default values and correctly store and return all three test data patterns (0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555). All SII registers must read back the written pattern masked with their respective write masks. All PHY registers must read back the PHY test pattern masked with the PHY write mask (0x1FFF) in the correct 16-bit field. The test calls finish(err2 || err1) where a zero value indicates all comparisons passed.
Remarks: The testcase does not perform link training or enumeration; it directly accesses registers at their mapped addresses. PHY register access requires a prior write to the PHY reset control register to release the PHY from reset. PHY registers are 16-bit wide and require address-alignment-based extraction from 32-bit reads. The SII and PHY registers have restricted write masks that limit which bits can be written. All PCIE1 DBI macros, all SII macros, and all PHY hex addresses could not be mapped to canonical register names in the DBI specification because they belong to separate register domains (SII and PHY) not covered by the provided DBI spec file. The test uses three data patterns for write-read verification but the source code defines six patterns in chk_val[] array; only the first three are used due to the loop bound j<3.
